title: Mucho eggplant (Mucho F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Mucho eggplant is an F1 hybrid eggplant variety from East West Seed. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Mucho eggplant is an F1 hybrid eggplant variety, also sold or known as Mucho F1 or Mucho talong. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from East West Seed.

heroImage.alt: Rows of young eggplant on furrowed beds in Norzagaray, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Mucho eggplant is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Mucho F1 or Mucho talong, this is the same eggplant. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [eggplant variety finder](/crop-varieties/eggplant), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

The registry gives no day count or trial yield for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit eggplant fields most often: [eggplant fruit and shoot borer](/pests/eggplant-fruit-and-shoot-borer), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [damping off](/diseases/damping-off), [eggplant leafhopper](/pests/eggplant-leafhopper). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 55 to 60 days after transplanting (60 to 65 on the variety page).
**Fruit:** Glossy dark purple, long cylinder, 23 to 25 cm, 115 to 120 g, with a bright green calyx.
Still marketable 5 to 7 days after picking.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: launched by East West in 2020 with farmer results from Bukidnon and Negros Occidental (Agriculture Monthly), listed on East West's Philippine site. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual eggplant on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Mucho eggplant

Buyers in each market want their own talong: long and slim and dark purple in most of Luzon, rounder or striped in some towns. Pick a variety with bacterial wilt resistance, and plan for the fruit and shoot borer whatever you plant, because no variety on the market resists it. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: Is Mucho F1 the same as Mucho?
items.a: Yes. Mucho F1 is another name for Mucho. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Mucho?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
